```{r}
#| eval: false
barRoso::barroso_write_descriptions()
```

### Description

This function reads morphological data from an Excel spreadsheet,
generates standardized species descriptions in plain text and Word document formats,
and exports them to a Word (.docx) file. It handles complex morphological data
structures including measurements, subterms and grouping of related characters.
The function automatically detects measurement ranges and formats them with
en dashes (e.g., "4.3–14.5 cm"). Optionally, it can compute and print averages
for user-selected measurement columns when a species has more than a threshold
number of values (see `avg_cols` and `avg_min_n`).
Rare small and large values are written between parentheses, as usual in
taxonomic descriptions, e.g. "(2–)6–40(–55) m" (see `extremes`).

### Details

**Measurements**

Each cell of a measurement column has the measurements of one specimen. When a
specimen was measured more than once (e.g. several leaves), the values are
separated by a vertical bar, e.g. `"4.5 | 7 | 11 | 14"`. The values of all
specimens of a species are pooled to build its range.

Rare values are written between parentheses in two ways:

**Marked in the spreadsheet**Values written as in a description,
e.g. `"(5–)7–38(–45)"` or `"(2–)6 | 9 | 12"`, are always kept as
extremes when they are beyond the range of the other values.
**Automatic**With `extremes = c(0.1, 0.9)`, when a species has
at least `extremes_min_n` values, the range covers the values from the
10th to the 90th percentile, and the smallest and largest values outside it
are written between parentheses. The range limits are always measured values.
With fewer values, the range goes from the smallest to the largest value.

**Column naming conventions**

The function relies on a structured column naming system to parse and organize
morphological traits. Columns must follow these conventions:

**Main character groups**Use ALL CAPS for the primary category:
`HABIT`, `STIPULE`, `LEAF`, `INFLORESCENCE`,
`FLOWER`, `FRUIT`, `SEED`. These will become section headers.

**Simple characters**Lowercase descriptive terms after the main group.
Examples: `LEAF shape`, `LEAF margin`, `FLOWER symmetry`.
These will be appended directly after the lowercase group name.

**Hierarchical characters**Use ALL CAPS for subgroup terms.
Examples: `LEAF PETIOLE length (cm)`, `FLOWER SEPALS shape`.
The capitalized term (`PETIOLE`, `SEPALS`) is extracted once
and used as a subheading.

**Measurements**Include units in parentheses for automatic detection:
`LEAF length (cm)`, `STIPULE width (mm)`, `HABIT height (m)`.
Multiple measurements (e.g., length + width) are automatically combined
with "×" and the unit is placed at the end.

**Column name flexibility**Spaces, dots, or underscores can be used
as separators. All of the following are valid:

- `STIPULE length (mm)`
- `STIPULE.length.(mm)`
- `STIPULE_length_mm`
- `LEAF PETIOLE shape`
- `LEAF.PETIOLE.shape`

**Example dataset**

The package includes an example dataset `chars_dataset` containing
morphological data for 15 species of *Ouratea* (Ochnaceae) compiled from
herbarium specimens and field observations for a taxonomic revision. This dataset
demonstrates proper column naming conventions and can be used to test the function:

data(chars_dataset)
head(names(chars_dataset))

**Creating a template**

To create a properly formatted Excel template with all required columns for your
plant group, use the companion function `barroso_chars_template`.
This function generates a ready-to-use template based on your species list and
selected plant group (e.g., "Ochnaceae", "Asteraceae", "Orchidaceae",
"Leguminosae-Papilionoideae"), saving hours of manual column creation.

# Create a template for Ochnaceae
barroso_chars_template(
  species_df = my_species_list,
  plant_group = "Ochnaceae",
  filename = "Ochnaceae_template"
)

### Arguments

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| xlsx_path | Character. Path to the .xlsx file containing morphological data with properly structured column names (see Details for naming conventions). |
| species_cols | Character vector or integer indices. Column names or indices used to build the species header (e.g., c("Genus", "Species", "Author") or 1:3). These can be combined flexibly (e.g., a single "Scientific_name" column or separate Genus, Species, and Author columns). |
| character_cols | Character vector or integer indices. Column names or indices of morphological character columns (e.g., c("HABIT", "LEAF shape", "LEAF length (cm)") or 4:20). These must follow the naming conventions described in Details. |
| sheet | Character string or integer. Sheet name or index passed to `readxl::read_excel()`. Default is 1. |
| species_filter | Optional character vector of species names to filter. Only species matching these names will have descriptions generated. The names should match the species name as it appears when concatenating the `species_cols` columns (without authorship). |
| avg_cols | Optional character vector or integer indices of columns for which an average should be reported, displayed immediately after the existing range (e.g. "3–8 × 1–2 cm, average 5.5 × 1.5 cm"). Must be a subset of `character_cols`. Default `NULL` (no averages reported). |
| avg_min_n | Integer. Minimum number of non-empty observations per species required for an average to be reported. Averages are emitted only when the number of observed values is strictly greater than `avg_min_n`. Default `3` (i.e., need at least 4 values for averaging). |
| extremes | Numeric vector of two percentiles (between 0 and 1), or `NULL`. Values below the first or above the second percentile of a species are written between parentheses, e.g. "(2–)6–40(–55) m", when the species has at least `extremes_min_n` values. Use `NULL` to keep just the extremes marked in the spreadsheet. Default `c(0.1, 0.9)`. |
| extremes_min_n | Integer. Minimum number of values of a species before automatic extremes are used. Default `10`. |
| approx_char | Character string to use for approximate measurements when no variation is present (e.g., "ca." or "c."). Default is "ca.". Set to `NULL` to disable adding approximation. Examples: `"ca. 0.1 × 0.1 cm"` (no variation) vs `"1.3–2.5 × 0.6–1.1 cm"` (variation present, no "ca."). |
| font_family | Character string. Font family for the Word document. Default is "Times New Roman". Common options include "Arial", "Calibri", "Cambria". |
| font_size | Numeric. Font size in points. Default is 12. |
| species_bold | Logical. Whether to make species names bold. Default is TRUE. |
| species_italic | Logical. Whether to make species names italic. Default is TRUE (following botanical conventions). |
| group_bold | Logical. Whether to make group names (e.g., "Habit", "Leaf") bold. Default is TRUE. |
| group_italic | Logical. Whether to make group names italic. Default is FALSE. |
| description_bold | Logical. Whether to make description text bold. Default is FALSE. |
| description_italic | Logical. Whether to make description text italic. Default is FALSE. |
| verbose | Logical. Print progress messages. Default TRUE. |
| filename | Output file base name (without extension). Default NULL (uses Excel filename with "_descriptions" suffix). |
| dir | Output directory. Default NULL (uses Excel filename as directory name). |

### Value

Invisibly returns a data.frame with two columns:

- `species_name`: Full species name with authorship
- `description_plain`: Plain text description

The main output is a Word document (.docx) saved to the specified directory.

### Examples

```r
# Basic usage with example dataset
data(chars_dataset)

# First, save the example dataset to Excel
library(openxlsx)
write.xlsx(chars_dataset, "chars_dataset.xlsx")

# Generate descriptions using proper column selection
barroso_write_descriptions(
  xlsx_path = "chars_dataset.xlsx",
  species_cols = c("Genus", "Species", "Author"),  # Taxonomic identification
  character_cols = 19:131,  # Morphological character columns
  approx_char = "ca."  # Add "ca." to measurements without variation
)

# Generate descriptions with average calculation
barroso_write_descriptions(
  xlsx_path = "morphological_data.xlsx",
  species_cols = c("Genus", "Species", "Author"),
  character_cols = 4:20,
  avg_cols = c("LEAF length (cm)", "FRUIT length (cm)"),
  avg_min_n = 3,  # Calculate averages when n > 3 observations
  approx_char = "ca."
)

# Filter to specific species only
barroso_write_descriptions(
  xlsx_path = "morphological_data.xlsx",
  species_cols = c("Genus", "Species"),
  character_cols = 3:15,
  species_filter = c("Ouratea concinna", "Ouratea coarctata")
)

# Customize text formatting in Word output
barroso_write_descriptions(
  xlsx_path = "morphological_data.xlsx",
  species_cols = 1:3,
  character_cols = 4:25,
  font_family = "Arial",
  font_size = 11,
  species_bold = TRUE,
  species_italic = TRUE,
  group_bold = FALSE,
  group_italic = TRUE,
  description_bold = FALSE,
  description_italic = FALSE,
  filename = "MySpeciesDescriptions",
  dir = "Output"
)
```
